content.text: Build the tool you would want to use
A small, fully remote team making software for teams who care about craft. We are hiring across engineering, design and sales.

attrs.alt: A still from our team film: three people at a long desk, screens glowing in a dark room
attrs.caption: Inside the team — a short film about how we work.

content.text: On a quest for quality
Most software is built to be bought. We want to build software that is a pleasure to use every single day — where the details are considered, the defaults are right and nothing gets in the way.
That takes a particular kind of team: people with taste, who finish things, and who would rather ship one excellent feature than three adequate ones. If that sounds like you, read on.
Read how we hire →
Principles
We make tools for people who care how things are made, so we have to care as much.
Small releases, every day. Feedback beats speculation.
Two or three people own an area completely. Nobody waits for permission.
We hire across time zones and design our days around the overlap.
Decisions, specs and post-mortems live in writing so everyone can catch up.
Every interaction should feel instant. We measure it and we fix it.
Focus is what makes the yes good.
There is no QA team to hand things to. Quality is in the work.
When something breaks, we find out why and change the system.
A good decision today beats a perfect one next month.
Clear feedback, delivered with care, is a kindness.

Eleven principles we hire for and hold each other to. They are a description of how we already work, not a poster.
Build for the craftsperson.
Ship early, then ship again.
Small teams, high trust.
Fully remote, deliberately.
Write things down.
Speed is a feature.
Say no to most things.
Quality is everyone’s job.
Fix the cause, not the symptom.
Momentum over perfection.
Be kind, be direct.
Every role goes through the same four steps, and we tell you where you are at each one. Most processes take two to three weeks from first call to offer.
The work trial
Instead of a whiteboard, we pay you to work with us on a real problem for a few days. You see how we work; we see how you work. It is the best predictor either side has.
What we look for
Taste — you can tell good from almost good.
Ownership — you finish things.
Clear writing — most of our collaboration is written.
